stops.note: 'flame'; Romans called the bird itself phoenicopterus ('crimson-wing', from Greek), and Pliny reports the gourmet Apicius praising its tongue
flama plus the Germanic suffix -enc; Provence's Camargue wetlands hold one of Europe's main flamingo breeding colonies
the same form also meant 'Flemish', and the two words were long confused by association
taken from Portuguese or Spanish; Mark Catesby's Natural History of Carolina (1730s) later gave English readers an early painting of the American flamingo

current_meaning: a tall pink wading bird with a bent bill
